title.analysis: Prison as unlikely megabusiness reverses punishment into commercial incentives. Concrete national system and money paradox target crime/business/policy audience. title.script_alignment: Incarceration scale and public cost introduce private operation as a commercial opportunity. Convict-leasing history leads to a simplified wage-rule account. License plates illustrate labor, bed guarantees introduce capacity incentives, and phone commissions monetize captive demand. Fixed-price healthcare creates a potential incentive to withhold care; Corizon restructuring extends the financial-engineering theme. The ending calls incarcerated people valuable customers. The incentive catalog is coherent, but legal programs, public spending and private profit are often conflated. The stored ending is complete.
